quotes.text: If an `Invoice` has an amount due, Stripe creates a *PaymentIntent*
For subscriptions that charge automatically, Stripe charges the default payment method on the subscription or customer.
The Accounts v2 API is generally available for Connect users, and in public preview for other Stripe users.
You can determine which features to provision for a customer by [retrieving their active entitlements or listening to the Active Entitlement Summary event]
When your customer completes the session, Stripe creates the subscription, creates a customer if you didn’t provide one, and collects any payment that’s due.

old_evidence.text: Stripe then creates the customer, activates the subscription, and handles payment
The Accounts v2 API is generally available for Connect users, and in public preview for other Stripe users.

findings: Same captured URL, https://docs.stripe.com/billing/billing-apis; new raw is the 2026-11-07 snapshot, old raw the 2026-05-12 snapshot. Current source is a May summary and must retain dated provenance while linking the new capture as new evidence.

New raw line 25 says Subscription→Invoice each cycle and describes PaymentIntent creation when the invoice has an amount due, tracked in the invoice payments list; automatic collection charges a subscription or customer default method. In the same 2026-11-07 capture, the PaymentIntent definition at line 190 says without qualification that invoices automatically create PaymentIntents. The May raw line 43 also uses that broad wording. This is an unresolved contradiction within the November snapshot, not proof of a universal runtime rule. Current source lines 13, 17 and 29 and wiki/concepts/stripe-subscriptions.md:14 all state the broad chain and require a qualified warning.

New raw lines 9-21 retain Product, Price and a customer-configured Account or Customer as subscription object relationships, with Accounts v2 general availability for Connect, preview/version requirement for other Stripe users, and a new Dashboard preview enablement instruction. This is documentation of variant/access prerequisites, not proof of account eligibility.

New raw lines 29-177 expand both Accounts v2 and Customer v1 diagrams into text. The example fields customer_account versus customer identify alternate model variants; sample active, open and processing statuses do not establish a completed payment or general lifecycle guarantee.

New raw lines 179-208 preserve the 11-object reference and entitlements example substantially. It says retrieve active entitlements or listen to the Active Entitlement Summary event for provisioning. Current source line 40's customer.activeEntitlements accessor is not evidenced in either capture.

New raw lines 210-212 move and qualify the Checkout Sessions recommendation: on completed session, creates subscription, creates a customer if none was supplied, and collects payment if due. The old line 8 said Stripe creates customer and activates subscription, which must remain dated and must not be carried forward as an unconditional current claim.
substantive_changes: The November billing narrative adds an amount-due condition for PaymentIntent creation, invoice payments list tracking, and default-method source for automatic collection (new line 25 versus old line 10). The same November object-definition table at line 190 retains a broad automatic-creation statement, so the conditional narrative is a changed presentation of the rule with an unresolved internal contradiction, not independently verified universal runtime behavior.
Checkout outcome and identity wording: customer created only if none provided, collects payment only if due, and no unconditional activation assertion (new line 212 versus old line 8).
Accounts v2 preview Dashboard enablement action is now explicit, while Connect GA/non-Connect preview and preview-version boundaries persist (new lines 17-21 versus old lines 20-24).
historical_claims_to_preserve: May 2026 raw lines 10 and 43 and current source lines 13, 17 and 29 contain an unconditional Invoice→PaymentIntent formulation. Retain the May wording as dated evidence and recognize that the November table at line 190 continues the broad formulation even though the November narrative at line 25 is conditional; do not assert either as a separately verified universal runtime rule.
May 2026 raw line 8 says Checkout creates the customer and activates the subscription; preserve as historical snapshot wording, not an outcome guaranteed by November line 212.
Accounts v2 Connect GA, other-user public preview and preview-version requirement appear in both dated captures; preserve those scope qualifications (old line 20, new line 17).
conflicts: Internal November conflict: raw line 25 conditions PaymentIntent creation on an invoice having an amount due, whereas raw line 190 says invoices automatically create PaymentIntents without that qualification. Old raw line 43 preserves the broad table statement. Current source lines 13, 17 and 29 and wiki/concepts/stripe-subscriptions.md:14 repeat a broad chain. The source update and reciprocal concept route should explicitly warn about the within-capture tension and avoid choosing a universal runtime rule from this evidence alone.

Current source line 40 states check customer.activeEntitlements; new raw line 208 and old raw line 61 instead say retrieve active entitlements or listen to Active Entitlement Summary event. Remove unsupported accessor claim.

Current source line 33 says Entitlement auto-created when subscription starts, while both raw tables tie creation to creating a subscription for a recurring service product with associated features (old line 40, new line 187). Narrow wording to feature-associated subscriptions.
unresolved_questions: The capture does not verify actual Accounts v2 preview enrollment or version availability for any particular merchant account.
The overview does not resolve payment finality or exact subscription status after a completed Checkout Session; the old activation statement conflicts with the new, narrower outcome wording.
The text diagram's example status values are illustrative and cannot establish a live transaction or universal status transition.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/billing/billing-apis, the November capture connects a subscription to Product, Price, and either a customer-configured Account or Customer (new lines 9-13). Its billing narrative says an invoice is generated each cycle and a PaymentIntent is created if the invoice has an amount due, tracked in invoice payments (new line 25). Yet its own object table says invoices automatically create PaymentIntents without that condition (new line 190), as did the May table (old line 43) and May narrative (old line 10). [[source-stripe-billing-apis]] lines 13, 17 and 29 repeat the broad claim. Accounts v2 remains Connect GA and preview otherwise with a version condition (new line 17; old line 20). The source and reciprocal wiki/concepts/stripe-subscriptions.md:14 route should flag the unresolved within-capture tension rather than claim universal runtime behavior.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/billing/billing-apis, the substantive November changes include the amount-due condition and invoice payments list in the billing narrative (new line 25 versus old line 10), but the same November table retains the unqualified PaymentIntent statement (new line 190; old table line 43). [[source-stripe-billing-apis]] should preserve both and warn about the conflict across its broad lines 13, 17 and 29, with a reciprocal qualification at wiki/concepts/stripe-subscriptions.md:14. Checkout now says it creates a customer only if none was supplied and collects payment if due, without the old unconditional activation wording (new line 212; old line 8). Accounts v2 preview enablement is explicit (new line 19); expanded variant diagrams and list formatting are presentation, while the entitlements link and See also entries are navigation (new 29-177, 208, 214-218). The source's unsupported customer.activeEntitlements accessor (line 40) needs correction. Example statuses and Checkout completion establish neither payment finality nor account eligibility.
